info.name: Marketplace_https
info.description:
# Marketplace API — Test Collection

## Environment variables

The collection relies on the following variables. Set `baseUrl` before running; all other variables are populated automatically by test scripts as the collection progresses.

| Variable | Set by | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | You | Base URL of the API, e.g. `https://localhost:5001` |
| `jwt` | Register / Login scripts | The **active** JWT used by the current request context |
| `activeRole` | User A, B, C flows | Identifier to show activer user(Seller, buyer or attacker) |
| `listingId` | Create listing | ID of the listing created by the Seller |
| `conversationId` | Create conversation | ID of the conversation opened by the Buyer |

## Recommended run order

Folders **must** be executed in the order listed below. Each folder produces environment variables consumed by later folders.

```
1. User A - Seller          → registers, logs in, creates a listing
2. User B - Buyer           → registers, logs in, starts a conversation & messaging
3. User A - Seller          → seller replies and fetches messages
4. User C - Attacker        → registers, then attempts unauthorized actions
5. User D - 2FA tests       → standalone 2FA flow (can run independently)
6. Validation tests         → standalone input-validation tests (can run independently)
7. Get all listings         → Can only run if any listings exist

 ```

## Notes

- All requests use HTTPS (`{{baseUrl}}` should point to a TLS-enabled host).

item.name: User A - Seller

formdata.value: Used car, but drives like brand new.

item.description:
## User A — Seller

**Purpose:** Establishes the Seller identity and creates the core data (listing) that subsequent folders depend on.

**Run order within this folder:**

1. `Register User (Seller)` — creates the seller account; stores `sellerJwt`
    
2. `Login (Seller)` — re-authenticates and refreshes `sellerJwt` / `jwt`
    
3. `Create listing (Seller)` — creates a "Fiat 500" listing; stores `listingId`
    
4. `Create conversation (Invalid)` — verifies a seller **cannot** open a conversation on their own listing (expects 400)
    
5. `Get messages (Authorized)` — reads the message thread (empty at this point; expects 200 + array)
    
6. `Send message (Seller → Buyer)` — seller sends a reply after the buyer has initiated the conversation _(run this after User B folder)_
    
7. `Delete listing (Authorized)` — cleans up the listing created in step 3
    
8. `Delete User (Seller)` \- removes the user completely along with all related data
    

**Note:** Step 3, requires an valid CategoryId from the database and insert image file from own computer.

**Environment side-effects:** `sellerJwt`, `jwt`, `listingId`

item.name: User B - Buyer

exec: pm.expect(json.text).to.eql("Hello, is this item still available?");

item.description:
## User B — Buyer

**Purpose:** Establishes the Buyer identity, initiates a conversation on the Seller's listing, and exercises the messaging flow from the buyer's perspective.

**Run order within this folder:**

1. `Register (Buyer)` — creates the buyer account; stores `buyerJwt`
    
2. `Login (Buyer)` — re-authenticates and refreshes `buyerJwt` / `jwt`
    
3. `Create conversation (Buyer → Seller)` — opens a conversation on `{{listingId}}`; stores `conversationId`
    
4. `Send message (Buyer → Seller)` — sends the opening message ("Hello, is this item still available")
    
5. `Get messages (Authorized)` — verifies the sent message is present in the thread
    
6. `Delete User (Buyer)` - removes the user completely along with all related data
    

**Depends on:** `listingId` set by User A folder.  
**Environment side-effects:** `buyerJwt`, `jwt`, `conversationId`

item.name: User C - Attacker
item.description:
## User C — Attacker

**Purpose:** Verifies that authorization boundaries are enforced. The Attacker is a legitimately registered user who attempts to access resources they do not own.

**Run order within this folder:**

1. `Register User (Attacker)` — creates the attacker account; stores `attackerJwt`
    
2. `Login (Attacker)` — re-authenticates and refreshes `attackerJwt` / `jwt`
    
3. `Get messages (Unauthorized)` — tries to read `{{conversationId}}` (owned by Buyer/Seller); expects 401 or 403
    
4. `Delete listing (Unauthorized)` — tries to delete `{{listingId}}` (owned by Seller); expects 401 or 403
    
5. `Delete User (Attacker)` - removes the user completely along with all related data
    

**Depends on:** `conversationId` (User B) and `listingId` (User A).  
**Environment side-effects:** `attackerJwt`, `jwt`

item.name: User D - 2FA tests
item.description:
## User D — 2FA Tests

**Purpose:** Validates the two-factor authentication (TOTP) setup and OTP validation flow. This folder is largely self-contained and can be run independently of Users A–C.

**Run order within this folder:**

1. `Register User` — creates account; stores `jwt`
    
2. `Setup 2FA` — requests a TOTP QR code; response must contain `qrCodeImage`
    
3. `Login` — authenticates the user
    
4. `Validate otp` — submits a TOTP code; expects HTTP 200 and a valid JWT
    
5. `Delete User` - removes the user completely along with all related data
    

**Note:**

Step 2: Scan the qr code with an Authenticator app (e.g. Microsoft Authenticator). You will need to login afterwards, and now Two Factor Authentication is required. It will give you a temporary JWT-token, that last 5 minutes, that can be used with the `Validate otp` request.

Step 3 requires a real TOTP code. This step will need a valid OTP value injected (Use Authenticator app e.g. Microsoft Authenticator).

**Environment side-effects:** `jwt`

item.description:
## Validation Tests — Input Validation

**Purpose:** Verifies that the API enforces input validation rules and returns appropriate error codes for bad input. These tests are stateless and can be run independently.

**Requests:**

- `Login - Wrong password` — sends correct email(If User A exists) but wrong password; expects 401 or 403
    
- `Register - Invalid email format` — sends a invalid email address format during registration; expects HTTP 400
